text:
How do you know if Google Ads is right for you?

Three questions.

Do people search for what you do?
Is a new customer worth a decent amount to you?
Can you take on more work this month?

Three yeses, I'd be running ads. A no on the last one, I'd wait.

Three things that help a local business rank higher on Google:

1. A complete Business Profile with the right main category.
2. A steady flow of real reviews.
3. A page on your website for each service you want to be found for.

None of it's quick. All of it compounds.

A bathroom renovator in Rockingham, open eight months. The bloke down the road, going 20 years.

His last Google review was from 2021. His website hasn't changed since the iPhone 6.

Guess who's climbing the map.

Google rewards whoever's putting in the work now.

Google Ads works like a tap.

Turn it on and people searching right now see you. Turn it off and it stops.

Perfect when a dentist in Toowong has empty chairs next week.

Pointless if your diary's full until February. You'd be paying for calls you can't take.

Google's own help page on local rankings says there's no way to request or pay for a better spot on the map.

So the businesses at the top got there the slow way. Proper profile. Useful pages. Patience.

Here's how I did it for my own business:
https://gimsresults.com.au/post/perth-seo-expert-ranked-own-business

The ranking factor most tradies leave on the table: reviews.

Google says more reviews and positive ratings can improve your local ranking.

Easiest time to ask is the minute the job's done. Customer's happy, hot water's running, phone's in hand.

Text the link before you leave.
